examples.cn: 电话打着打着就没电了。

examples.en: We stopped at a dead end and turned back.
examples.cn: 我们在死胡同前停下，掉头回去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dead 记成「呆的」：呆着一动不动，就是没有生气了。

root: 源自古英语 dēad，与古诺尔斯语 dauðr 等同源，更早可上溯到印欧语中表示「死去」的词根；十四世纪起从身体扩展到工具与语言，副词用法又引申出「彻底、正好」的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a body without life, to a machine without power, to a word meaning completely.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有生命的身体，到没有电的机器，再到表示彻底的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird on a sill that never moves again.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗台上一只再不动的鸟。

branches.en: The first sense is the biological line that cannot be crossed back.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那条无法回头跨过的生理界线。

branches.en: The second lends that stillness to anything that has stopped.
branches.cn: 第二个把这种静止借给一切停下来的东西。

branches.en: The third turns the end point into a measure of completeness.
branches.cn: 第三个把终点变成一种彻底的程度。

branches.en: A dead battery and a dead bird share only the stillness.
branches.cn: 没电的电池和死去的鸟，只共享那份静止。

branches.en: Going dead and going all the way are the same direction.
branches.cn: 「停死」和「走到底」是同一个方向。

intro.en: Dead is a small but productive family, with nouns and verbs built on the idea of stopped life.
intro.cn: dead 这一族不大却能产词，名词和动词都建在「生命停住」这个意思上。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; dead is a native Germanic adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不涉及拉丁词根，dead 是本族日耳曼形容词。

items.example: The leaves are dead.
His death was sudden.
The snake is deadly.

items.meaning: to make less strong or less felt
items.example: The walls deaden the noise.

items.meaning: the state of being without life
items.example: A strange deadness filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 屋里充满一种奇怪的死寂。

items.meaning: a road or plan with no way on
items.example: The job was a dead end.
Latin is a dead language.
The arrow hit dead centre.

definition_en: the latest time by which something must be finished
core_image: 墙上的钟快指到午夜，桌上还堆着没写完的稿子
scene: 编辑在日历上圈出周五，说那天必须交稿。The deadline is Friday at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 deadline 指「截止期限」（第 1 个义项：必须完成某事的最晚时间）；句意是截止时间是周五中午。

senses.title: The last moment allowed
senses.definition: the fixed time after which work is no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 过了这个时间，工作就不再被接受
senses.example: The deadline is Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 截止时间是周五中午。
senses.why: A line drawn across time works like a line drawn on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上画的一条线，和在地上画的一条线一样管用。

senses.title: A line one must not cross
senses.definition: the original sense: a boundary in a prison camp that guards would shoot across
senses.definitionCN: 最初的义项：战俘营里一道越过去就会被开枪射击的界线
senses.example: The old prison deadline was marked with white stones.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧战俘营的界线是用白石标出的。
senses.why: The word began as a line you crossed only once, and time borrowed its force.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一条只能越一次的线，时间借走了它的力量。

intro.en: Deadline first named a real line on the ground in an American prison camp during the civil war.
intro.cn: deadline 最初指美国内战时期战俘营地上一条真实的界线。

items.en: A deadline was a line past which prisoners would be shot.
items.cn: deadline 指战俘越过就会被射杀的界线。

items.en: Printers used the word for a line of type beyond the page.
items.cn: 印刷工用它指超出页面的一道字行。

items.en: Newspapers used deadline for the hour a story had to be in.
items.cn: 报社用它指稿件必须交到的钟点。

items.en: The word spread from newsrooms into every kind of work.
items.cn: 这个词从新闻编辑室扩散到各行各业。

items.en: A deadline is now any moment that ends the time allowed.
items.cn: 如今 deadline 指任何结束允许时间的时刻。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dead- or -line shape, and the meaning group names other ends of time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dead- 或 -line 的词形，近义组则列出时间的其他终点。

entries.definition: no longer alive or working
entries.definitionCN: 不再活着或不再运转的

entries.definition: a long thin mark
a state where neither side can move
entries.definitionCN: 双方都无法前进的僵局

entries.definition: the point at which something stops being allowed
entries.definitionCN: 某事不再被允许的那个点

entries.definition: the greatest amount or point permitted
entries.definitionCN: 被允许的最大量或最远点

entries.definition: the day on which something must be handed in
entries.definitionCN: 必须交上某物的那一天

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line on prison ground and end with a clock that refuses to wait.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从战俘营地上的一条线开始，落到一只不肯等人的钟。

normal.en: A deadline is a wall built out of minutes.
normal.cn: 截止期，是用分钟砌起来的一堵墙。

normal.en: The word once meant a line you could not walk past.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指一条不能走过去的线。

normal.en: Work stretches until a deadline gives it a shape.
normal.cn: 工作一直拖着，直到截止期给它一个形状。

normal.en: A missed deadline is louder than a late excuse.
normal.cn: 错过的截止期，比迟到的解释更响。

normal.en: The clock does not move faster; only the room does.
normal.cn: 钟没有走快，是屋里的人变快了。

abstract.en: Picture a clock on a wall and a page still blank.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只钟，桌上还是一张白纸。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a folder across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把文件夹推过柜台。

abstract.en: Picture white stones laid in a straight line on bare ground.
abstract.cn: 想象空地上用白石摆出的一条直线。

examples.en: The deadline is Friday at noon.
examples.cn: 截止时间是周五中午。

examples.en: They worked all night to meet the deadline.
examples.cn: 为了赶上截止期，他们干了一整夜。

examples.en: The editor agreed to extend the deadline by a week.
examples.cn: 编辑同意把截止期延长一周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deadline 记成「死线」：dead 是死，line 是线，一条过了就完了的线，就是截止期。

root: 由 dead（死的）与 line（线）复合而成，十九世纪六十年代美国战俘营里指越界即被射杀的界线；印刷业与报社先后借用，二十世纪起泛指一切必须完成工作的最后时刻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line on the ground you must not cross, to a line on the clock you must not pass.
sensesIntro.cn: 从地上不能越过的线，到钟上不能越过的线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn across time with a clock behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：横在时间上的一条线，身后是一只钟。

branches.en: The first sense is the modern one: the last accepted moment.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是现代义：最后被接受的那一刻。

branches.en: The second is the literal line that gave the word its force.
branches.cn: 第二个是给这个词以力量的那条真实的线。

branches.en: Both senses share one rule: past this point, there is no return.
branches.cn: 两个义项共用一条规矩：过了这点，就回不去了。

branches.en: The prison line became a metaphor the moment offices needed one.
branches.cn: 办公室一需要比喻，战俘营的那条线就变成了比喻。

branches.en: A deadline is frightening because it remembers being deadly.
branches.cn: 截止期之所以吓人，是因为它记得自己曾经致命。

intro.en: Deadline is a compound, so its family is built by pairing it with the verbs and nouns of work.
intro.cn: deadline 是复合词，它的一族靠与工作相关的动词和名词搭配而成。

latinIntro.en: The two halves are native English: dead from Old English dēad, line from Latin linea through French.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都算英语本族：dead 出自古英语 dēad，line 则经法语来自拉丁语 linea。

items.example: The deadline is close.
The plant is dead.
Draw a line here.
They met the deadline easily.

items.meaning: to fail to finish in time
items.example: He missed the deadline by a day.

items.meaning: a deadline that leaves little time
items.example: She works well under a tight deadline.
items.exampleCN: 期限紧迫时她反而干得好。

items.meaning: the stress caused by a deadline
items.example: Deadline pressure kept him at his desk.
items.exampleCN: 截止期的压力把他按在桌前。

items.example: The bank extended the deadline.

definition_en: unable to hear, or refusing to listen
core_image: 一个人把手掌贴在耳后，仍然听不见
scene: 老人把手拢在耳后，还是听不清孙子的声音。The old man has been deaf since childhood.
sceneCN: 这里 deaf 指「聋的」（第 1 个义项：听不见声音的）；句意是这位老人从小就聋。

senses.title: Unable to hear
senses.definition: having little or no ability to hear sounds
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有或完全没有听见声音的能力
senses.example: The old man has been deaf since childhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老人从小就聋。
senses.why: The word describes the ear, not the sound; the sound is still there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词说的是耳朵，不是声音；声音一直都在。

senses.title: Refusing to listen
senses.definition: choosing not to pay attention to advice or appeals
senses.definitionCN: 选择不去理会劝告或请求
senses.example: He was deaf to every warning we gave.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的每一次警告他都听不进去。
senses.why: We borrow the ear's condition to describe the will's refusal.
senses.whyCN: 我们借耳朵的状况，来形容意志的拒绝。

intro.en: Deaf is an Old English adjective, dēaf, with close relatives in Dutch and German.
intro.cn: deaf 是古英语形容词 dēaf，在荷兰语和德语里都有近亲。

items.en: A root suggesting dullness of sense lies behind the word.
items.cn: 这个词背后有一个表示感官迟钝的词根。

items.en: Dēaf meant unable to hear, and also dull or empty.
items.cn: dēaf 既指听不见，也指迟钝或空。

items.en: Norse daufr kept the same sense of not hearing.
items.cn: 诺尔斯语 daufr 保留了听不见的意思。

items.en: The figurative sense, deaf to advice, became common.
items.cn: deaf to advice 这类比喻用法变得常见。

items.en: Deaf now names both a condition and a refusal.
items.cn: 如今 deaf 既指一种状况，也指一种拒绝。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short e and final consonant, and the meaning group names ways of not responding.
note.cn: 形近组共享短元音 e 和词尾辅音，近义组则列出不回应的方式。

entries.definition: no longer alive
to give out cards or to handle a matter
loved or expensive
not able to hear well
not reacting to words or actions
entries.definitionCN: 对言语或行动没有反应的

entries.definition: paying no attention to warnings

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand cupped behind an ear and end with a warning that nobody answers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从拢在耳后的那只手开始，落到一句没人回应的警告。

normal.en: Deaf describes the ear; the world still speaks.
normal.cn: deaf 说的是耳朵，世界仍在说话。

normal.en: A deaf ear and a closed mind use the same word.
normal.cn: 聋的耳朵和关上的心，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: The word once also meant dull, as if the senses had gone quiet.
normal.cn: 这个词从前也指迟钝，仿佛感官安静了下来。

normal.en: Silence in a deaf room is not empty; it is full.
normal.cn: 聋人房里的安静并不空，它是满的。

normal.en: Turn a deaf ear and you choose to lose a warning.
normal.cn: 置若罔闻，就是选择丢掉一次警告。

abstract.en: Picture a hand cupped behind an ear in a crowded room.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的屋里，一只手拢在耳后。

abstract.en: Picture a mouth moving and no sound arriving.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴在动，声音却没有到达。

abstract.en: Picture eyes doing all the work the ears once did.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛在做耳朵从前做的所有事。

examples.en: The old man has been deaf since childhood.
examples.cn: 这位老人从小就聋。

examples.en: She is deaf in one ear after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后她一只耳朵聋了。

examples.en: He turned a deaf ear to their advice.
examples.cn: 他对他们的劝告置若罔闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deaf 记成「得夫」：耳朵听不见，只能靠眼睛「得」到信息，就像少了半边天。

root: 源自古英语 dēaf（听不见、迟钝），与荷兰语 doof、德语 taub 同源，更早可上溯到一个表示感官迟钝的印欧词根；中古英语起引申出「不愿听」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: From an ear that cannot catch sound, to a will that will not catch advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 从接不住声音的耳朵，到接不住劝告的意志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand cupped behind an ear that still hears nothing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手拢在耳后，仍什么也听不见。

branches.en: The first sense is a physical limit of the ear.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是耳朵的生理限制。

branches.en: The second is a chosen limit of attention.
branches.cn: 第二个是主动选择的注意力限制。

branches.en: Both describe a door that does not open when someone knocks.
branches.cn: 两者都形容一扇有人敲却不开的门。

branches.en: The metaphor works because the condition is familiar.
branches.cn: 这个比喻成立，是因为那种状况人人熟悉。

branches.en: One is not a choice; the other is nothing but choice.
branches.cn: 一个是无从选择，一个纯粹是选择。

intro.en: Deaf has a small family of verbs, adjectives, and fixed phrases, all built on not hearing.
intro.cn: deaf 有一小族动词、形容词和固定短语，全都建立在「听不见」上。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; deaf is a native Germanic adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，deaf 是本族日耳曼形容词。

items.example: The child was born deaf.
The explosion deafened him for a day.

items.meaning: so loud it blocks all other sound
items.example: The noise was deafening.
Deafness did not stop her work.
items.exampleCN: 失聪没有让她停下工作。

items.meaning: an old name for a hearing aid
items.example: He wore a deaf aid in one ear.
items.exampleCN: 他一只耳朵戴着助听器。

items.example: They were deaf to our appeals.
items.exampleCN: 他们对我们的请求充耳不闻。

items.example: She turned a deaf ear to the rumours.
His grandfather is stone deaf.

definition_en: to take action about something, or an agreement between two sides
core_image: 两人在桌边交换文件，然后握手成交
scene: 双方在桌边握了手，一笔买卖就这么定了。They shook hands to close the deal.
sceneCN: 这里 deal 指「交易」（第 1 个义项：双方达成的买卖或协议）；句意是他们握手成交。

senses.title: An agreement between two sides
senses.definition: an arrangement in business or politics that both sides accept
senses.definitionCN: 商业或政治中双方都接受的安排
senses.example: They shook hands to close the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们握手成交。
senses.why: A deal is a division that both sides agree to call fair.
senses.whyCN: 交易，是双方都愿意称之为公平的一种分配。

senses.title: To handle a matter
senses.definition: to take action about a problem or a person
senses.definitionCN: 对一个问题或一个人采取行动
senses.example: She knows how to deal with angry customers.
senses.exampleCN: 她知道怎样应对发火的顾客。
senses.why: Handling a problem is handing out the parts of it one by one.
senses.whyCN: 处理问题，就是把它的各部分一件件分派出去。

senses.title: A large amount
senses.definition: a great quantity, as in a great deal of time
senses.definitionCN: 很大的数量，如大量的时间
senses.example: It took a great deal of courage to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 开口需要极大的勇气。
senses.why: A share divided many times becomes an amount too large to count.
senses.whyCN: 一份被分了很多次，就成了数不清的量。

intro.en: Deal goes back to Old English dǣlan, to divide, and every sense still carries a share of that.
intro.cn: deal 可上溯到古英语 dǣlan（分开），每个义项里都还留着「分」的影子。

items.en: Dǣlan meant to divide something among people.
items.cn: dǣlan 意为把东西分给众人。

items.en: The noun named the portion each person received.
items.cn: 名词指每个人分到的那一份。

items.en: Deal came to mean doing business by exchanging shares.
items.cn: deal 开始指通过交换份额来做买卖。

items.en: Cards gave the word its sense of handing out what is held.
items.cn: 纸牌给了这个词「把手上的东西发出去」的意思。

items.en: A great deal of later turned the idea of shares into mere quantity.
items.cn: 后来 a great deal of 把「份额」变成了纯粹的数量。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the long e and final consonant, and the meaning group names other business and coping words.
note.cn: 形近组共享长元音 e 与词尾辅音，近义组则列出其他生意与应对的说法。

entries.definition: unable to hear
loved or expensive
the food eaten at one time
an agreement with better terms than usual
entries.definitionCN: 条件比寻常更合算的协议

entries.definition: an act of buying or selling
to manage a situation or a person
entries.definitionCN: 应付某种局面或某个人

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thing broken into shares and end with a problem taken apart the same way.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被分成几份的东西开始，落到以同样方式拆开的问题。

normal.en: To deal is to divide, whether goods or trouble.
normal.cn: deal 就是分，分货物，也分麻烦。

normal.en: Cards are dealt because a hand of cards is a share.
normal.cn: 牌要发出去，因为一手牌就是一份。

normal.en: A fair deal is one both sides can call dividing fairly.
normal.cn: 公平的交易，是双方都愿意称作分得公道。

normal.en: A great deal of time is time cut into too many pieces to count.
normal.cn: 大量的时间，是时间被切成了数不清的碎片。

normal.en: The word has never lost the idea of a hand passing something on.
normal.cn: 这个词始终没有丢掉「一只手把东西递过去」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture two hands meeting above a signed page.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在签好字的纸上方相握。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of cards split into two even piles.
abstract.cn: 想象一副牌被分成两叠一样高。

abstract.en: Picture a problem laid out on a table in separate parts.
abstract.cn: 想象一个难题被拆成几块摊在桌上。

examples.en: They shook hands to close the deal.
examples.cn: 他们握手成交。

examples.en: She knows how to deal with angry customers.
examples.cn: 她知道怎样应对发火的顾客。

examples.en: It took a great deal of courage to speak.
examples.cn: 开口需要极大的勇气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deal 记成「地儿」：找对地方谈生意，分好各自的地儿，买卖就谈成了。

root: 源自古英语 dǣlan（分开、分配），与德语 teilen 同源；中古英语由「分得的一份」引申为买卖与协议，纸牌又带来「发牌」之义，后来 a great deal of 又把份额抽象成数量。

sensesIntro.en: From dividing a thing into shares, to the agreement about those shares, to a problem shared out and handled.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西分成份，到就这些份达成协议，再到把问题拆开应付。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting over a page that divides something.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在一张分配东西的纸上相握。

branches.en: The first sense is the agreement that makes the division fair.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是让这次分配显得公平的协议。

branches.en: The second applies the same dividing to a problem.
branches.cn: 第二个把同样的「分」用在问题上。

branches.en: The third keeps only the size of the share, not its fairness.
branches.cn: 第三个只留下份额的大小，不再管公平。

branches.en: A good negotiator and a good manager do the same thing.
branches.cn: 好的谈判者和好的管理者做的是同一件事。

branches.en: Handling a lot of work is dealing out a great deal of effort.
branches.cn: 应付大量工作，就是分发大量的力气。

intro.en: Deal is a productive verb, and its family grows through -er, -ing, and a set of phrasal patterns.
intro.cn: deal 是个能产词的动词，一族靠 -er、-ing 和一批短语长出来。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root stands behind deal; it is a native Germanic verb from Old English dǣlan.
latinIntro.cn: deal 背后没有拉丁词根，它是古英语 dǣlan 传下来的本族日耳曼动词。

items.example: Who deals the cards tonight?

items.meaning: one who buys, sells, or gives out
items.example: The dealer showed us two cars.
items.exampleCN: 经销商给我们看了两辆车。

items.meaning: business activity or treatment of others
items.example: Their dealings were always honest.

items.meaning: a shop allowed to sell a brand
items.example: The dealership opened in May.

items.meaning: to handle or take action about
items.example: I will deal with the letters today.

items.meaning: to trade in a kind of goods
items.example: They deal in old books.

items.meaning: to give out to each person
items.example: He dealt out the papers.
A great deal depends on the weather.

definition_en: a person or business that buys and sells goods, or one who gives out cards
core_image: 车行里挂着钥匙、笑着迎人的销售员
scene: 车行老板把钥匙放在柜台上，报了一个价。The dealer offered a lower price.
sceneCN: 这里 dealer 指「经销商」（第 1 个义项：买卖某类商品的人或商号）；句意是经销商报了一个更低的价。

senses.title: A person who trades
senses.definition: someone whose business is buying and selling a kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 以买卖某类商品为业的人
senses.example: The dealer offered a lower price.
senses.exampleCN: 经销商报了一个更低的价。
senses.why: The suffix -er turns the act of dealing into a person who lives by it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 把「做买卖」这个动作，变成靠它生活的人。

senses.title: The one who gives out cards
senses.definition: the person who shares the cards among the players
senses.definitionCN: 在玩牌的人之间分牌的人
senses.example: The dealer turned over the first card.
senses.exampleCN: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。
senses.why: The oldest sense of dealing is feeding cards to the table.
senses.whyCN: dealing 最老的意思，就是给牌桌递牌。

intro.en: Dealer is deal plus -er, so it names whoever divides or hands out.
intro.cn: dealer 是 deal 加 -er 构成，指负责分配或递出东西的人。

items.en: The base verb meant to divide among people.
items.cn: 词根动词意为在众人之间分配。

items.en: A dealer was simply one who handed out shares.
items.cn: dealer 最初只指分份的人。

items.en: Card players gave the word its lasting use at the table.
items.cn: 打牌的人让这个词在牌桌上固定下来。

items.en: Dealer also named a merchant of one particular goods.
items.cn: dealer 也开始指经营某一类商品的商人。

items.en: Car dealer, art dealer, and drug dealer fixed the pattern.
items.cn: car dealer、art dealer 与 drug dealer 固定了这一模式。

note.en: The look-alike group ends in -aler, and the meaning group names others who move goods.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -aler 结尾，近义组则列出其他转手货物的人。

entries.definition: to divide or do business
a person who makes others well
a person who guides a group
a person who trades in goods on a large scale
entries.definitionCN: 大规模做货物买卖的人

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells for a living
a firm that provides goods to others

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand of cards spread on a table and end with a row of cars under bright lights.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从摊在桌上的一手牌开始，落到灯下一排亮闪闪的车。

normal.en: A dealer is the one who decides how the shares fall.
normal.cn: 经销商是决定份额怎么落下的人。

normal.en: The card table gave the word its first steady job.
normal.cn: 牌桌给了这个词第一份稳定的工作。

normal.en: Add -er to dealing and you have put a person in the shop.
normal.cn: 给 dealing 加 -er，店里就多了一个人。

normal.en: A good dealer knows the goods better than the buyer does.
normal.cn: 好商人比买家更懂自己的货。

normal.en: The word carries no judgement; the goods decide that.
normal.cn: 这个词本身不带评判，是货物在决定评判。

abstract.en: Picture a fan of cards sliding across green cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一把牌滑过绿绒桌面。

abstract.en: Picture keys hanging in rows behind a glass counter.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜台后一排排挂着的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture two men talking quietly beside a parked car.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在一辆停着的车旁低声交谈。

examples.en: The dealer offered a lower price.
examples.cn: 经销商报了一个更低的价。

examples.en: The dealer turned over the first card.
examples.cn: 发牌的人翻开第一张牌。

examples.en: They bought the van from a local dealer.
examples.cn: 他们从本地经销商那里买了那辆面包车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dealer 记成「递了」：deal 是分，-er 是人，把货一件件递出去的人就是经销商。

root: 由 deal（分配、交易）加施动后缀 -er 构成；中古英语时指分份的人，十六世纪因纸牌而固定为「发牌者」，十七世纪起又指经营某一类商品的商人。

sensesIntro.en: From the hand that shares out cards, to the shop that shares out goods.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分牌的那只手，到分发货物的那家店。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a share of something across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一份东西推过柜台。

branches.en: The first sense is a person whose living is the exchange itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是以交换本身为生的人。

branches.en: The second is the same hand, sharing cards instead of goods.
branches.cn: 第二个是同一只手，分的是牌而不是货。

branches.en: Both senses depend on giving each person a fair share.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠给每个人一份公道。

branches.en: The card table is the older picture under the shop.
branches.cn: 牌桌是商店底下那幅更老的画。

branches.en: A dealer never keeps the whole deck.
branches.cn: 经销商从不把整副牌都留下。

intro.en: Dealer is a person noun built on deal, and its compounds are named by the goods it handles.
intro.cn: dealer 是建在 deal 上的人称名词，复合词则按经手的货物来命名。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved; deal is native Germanic and -er is a Germanic agent ending.
latinIntro.cn: 不涉及拉丁词根：deal 是本族日耳曼词，-er 也是日耳曼语的施动后缀。

items.meaning: one who trades or gives out
items.example: The dealer knew every model.
items.exampleCN: 这位经销商熟悉每一款车。

items.example: They deal fairly.

items.meaning: a shop licensed to sell a brand
items.example: The dealership is on the ring road.
His dealings were always open.
The car dealer gave a warranty.

items.meaning: a trader in paintings and sculpture
items.example: An art dealer bought the sketch.
items.exampleCN: 一位艺术品商买下了那张草图。

items.meaning: the person who gives out cards
items.example: The card dealer smiled and shuffled.
items.exampleCN: 发牌的人笑了笑，开始洗牌。

items.meaning: a person who sells illegal drugs
items.example: The police caught the drug dealer.
items.exampleCN: 警方抓住了那个毒品贩子。
